anchor.quote: a base language, a compiler, a debugger, and a memory model

claims.rationale: The runtime vocabulary is the article's load-bearing Noesis frame, but the prose expressly denies metaphor and says Vedic texts document literal compiler and memory architecture. The house boundary and mathematical mechanism are therefore concealed.

legacy.quote: "a base language, a compiler, a debugger, and a memory model"
legacy.note: Declared structural conceit; consciousness-primary house frame framed openly as architecture, no external authority cited

anchor.quote: The Universal Runtime encompasses all executed states — past processes, active threads

claims.rationale: Rigveda 10.90 says Purusha is all that was and will be; “runtime,” processes, threads, privileges, and interfaces are Noesis software glosses presented as a translation. The source teaching, commentary, and synthesis are not separated.

legacy.quote: "The Universal Runtime encompasses all executed states — past processes, active threads"
legacy.note: Interpretive translation of Rigveda 10.90; content faithful (puruṣa as all that was/will be); historical-textual claim

anchor.quote: The three forces are not metaphorical energies. They are structural requirements.

claims.rationale: The Shikshavalli does not teach a Kha–Ba–La triad. The post launders a three-part Noesis architecture as the text's structural requirement without tracing ingredients, transformation, or authorship.

legacy.quote: "The three forces are not metaphorical energies. They are structural requirements."
legacy.note: Kha-Ba-La triad — house cosmology, ALIGNED by definition; structural grammar, not decoration

anchor.quote: Ask anyone who has woken from a three-day binge of work, consumption, or distraction

claims.rationale: “Ask anyone” generalizes a three-day binge and absent choice-memory without identifying an observer record, population, measure, or conditions. The duration adds nonconsequential specificity and has no provenance.

legacy.quote: "Ask anyone who has woken from a three-day binge of work, consumption, or distraction"
legacy.note: Direct reader-replicable observation; no institution invoked

anchor.quote: articulate every emotional pattern in their relationships but cannot feel their own feet

claims.rationale: The composite portrait of a person who can verbalize relationship patterns yet cannot feel their feet is presented as a recognizable dissociative pattern without a situated observation record or clinical source.

legacy.quote: "articulate every emotional pattern in their relationships but cannot feel their own feet"
legacy.note: Embodied observational marker; pattern the reader can verify directly

anchor.quote: causes them to revolve by a kind of mechanical power (maya)

claims.rationale: Bhagavad Gita 18.61 is accurately named and faithfully paraphrased as beings revolving as if mounted on a machine through maya; this is a source-teaching claim, not empirical proof.

legacy.quote: "causes them to revolve by a kind of mechanical power (maya)"
legacy.note: Accurate citation of Bhagavad Gita 18.61 (yantrārūḍhāni māyayā); judged as history/textual

anchor.quote: maps five sheaths — annamaya, pranamaya, manomaya, vijnanamaya, anandamaya

claims.rationale: The Taittiriya Upanishad is accurately identified as the source of the five koshas and the five names are correct. The count is provenance-traceable and structurally governs the article's nested-layer account.

legacy.quote: "maps five sheaths — annamaya, pranamaya, manomaya, vijnanamaya, anandamaya"
legacy.note: House Vedic framework; kosha enumeration correct (2.8 citation loosely spans 2.1–2.5 content; minor)

anchor.quote: Mātrā — measurement. The temporal quantization that makes sequence possible.

claims.rationale: The Shikshavalli lists varna, svara, matra, bala, sama, and santana as phonetic disciplines; “temporal quantization” and the six software-instruction glosses are an undeclared Noesis mapping, not the text's own technical grammar.

legacy.quote: "Mātrā — measurement. The temporal quantization that makes sequence possible."
legacy.note: Six-fold Shikshavalli list (varṇa, svara, mātrā, bala, sāma, santāna) is accurate; signal-processing glosses are declared analogy inside the explicit compiler conceit (§5 safe harbor), one-to-one mapping shown

anchor.quote: approximately 96 minutes before solar node activation

claims.rationale: Brahma Muhurta is traditionally placed two muhurtas before sunrise, so 2×48 minutes gives the stated approximately ninety-six minutes. The timing is correct, source-traceable within the named practice, and consequential to the morning protocol.

legacy.note: Brahma Muhurta arithmetic correct (2 muhurtas × 48 min before sunrise); house Vedic time-reckoning; "one ghati" (=24 min) also correct

claims.rationale: One muhurta is conventionally forty-eight minutes in the named Vedic time-reckoning. The equivalence is correct, provenance-traceable, and supplies the prescribed maintenance interval.

legacy.note: Muhurta arithmetic correct; house Vedic time unit

anchor.quote: multiplied by one hundred at each successive level of the five sheaths

claims.rationale: Taittiriya Upanishad 2.8 does use successive hundredfold joy measures, but its ananda ladder is a hierarchy of beings, not one multiplication for each of the five koshas. The numerical structure is attached to the wrong sequence.

legacy.quote: "multiplied by one hundred at each successive level of the five sheaths"
legacy.note: Taittiriya 2.8 ananda ladder ×100 is textually accurate; minor conflation — 2.8's ladder is the hierarchy of beings, not the kosha sequence

anchor.quote: The Quine principle applies: the system creates the conditions for its own transcendence

claims.rationale: A quine is a program that outputs its own source; no recognized “Quine principle” says a system creates conditions for self-transcendence. The name-drop is definitionally wrong and dispensable from the debugger analogy.

legacy.quote: "The Quine principle applies: the system creates the conditions for its own transcendence"
legacy.note: **DROSS.** No such principle exists: a quine is a self-reproducing program (Hofstadter naming Quine), and "self-transcendence" matches neither Quine's philosophy nor the quine concept. Definitionally false name-drop; sentence's real content is the raft parable, which stands without the name
